A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OneSearch study. All 14 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Kuaishou offline experiments, component ablations, online A/B tests, and manual evaluations in Sections 3–4.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds cold-start evaluation in Table 11 and a qualitative new-keyword test in Section 4.4.

M1.justification: The KHQE tokenizer, multi-view behavior injection, encoder-decoder architecture, and preference-aware training procedure remain the same. Revised aggregation formulas and Figure 4 labels clarify or correct the documented method without establishing an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: The Kuaishou dataset and search task remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds explicit evaluation of recently published, interaction-free items and users inactive for 90 days, plus a scenario with an injected novel keyword. v1 already discussed cold-start handling and tested catalog growth, but lacked these specific evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain OnlineMCA, its no-ranking variant, and the same tokenizer and OneSearch variants. The new cold-start comparison uses the existing OnlineMCA baseline; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated residual OPQ configuration for 4/256 from 512-512-256-256 to 256-256-256-256; this establishes a reported setting revision, not a rerun. New tests define seven-day interaction-free items and 90-day inactive users, and hold the codebook fixed during keyword injection. Existing splits, metrics, and main evaluation samples remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds warm-versus-cold item/user analyses and a qualitative test of SID generation after inserting a new keyword without rebuilding the codebook. The existing sequence ablations, tokenizer comparisons, catalog-growth analysis, and reasoning example are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Table 8's P-value-based coloring and the industry-analysis significance statements. Neither adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or a new statistical procedure. The new cold-start results have no accompanying uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes OnlineMCA MRR@10 from 0.1689 to 0.1323. Table 7's 4*4/256 row changes order MRR@10 and click HR@10/MRR@10 drops from -1.01/-3.00/-1.05% to -11.83/-27.11/-9.61%. Table 11 adds cold-item/user CTR gains of 3.31%/2.50% versus OnlineMCA; Section 4.4 reports successful SID generation after keyword injection. Figure 7 changes its MFU annotation from +700.38% to +24.06%, retaining the 3.26% and 27.32% endpoints. Main offline and online results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects the item-keyword sum's upper bound from m to n, matching its 1/n normalization. Equations (3)–(4) correct summation bounds and distinguish behavior-sequence lengths from hierarchy levels; the tensor-shape statement now refers to Q-Former's output Q. These are limited corrections to mathematical definitions, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about industrial end-to-end search, the three principal innovations, effectiveness, and efficiency. Added cold-start evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v5 newly concludes that OneSearch handles the defined cold-start populations well. It also interprets the keyword-injection observation as evidence that OPQ accommodates emerging keywords without rebuilding codebooks, giving additional motivation for real-time encoding. v1 already proposed real-time encoding as future work.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the documented codebook sizes for reproducing the 4/256 ablation. Section 3.2.3 clarifies per-level centroid aggregation and the Q-Former output, while Section 4.4 describes the fixed-codebook keyword-injection procedure. Main training hyperparameters, update schedules, and resource-access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 51 references and substantive related-work discussions are retained. Positioning against earlier generative retrieval, recommendation, and industrial search systems is unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized wording and cross-reference corrections, rewrites parts of the long-sequence explanation, expands Section 4.4 from three questions to four, and updates authors and contact information. The overall section structure and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v5 adds Table 11, adjusts labels and their arrangement in Figure 4, and reflows the expanded discussion and references. Existing tables and plots largely retain their structure and visual design.

improvement.justification: v5 adds targeted cold-start evidence absent from v1 and improves mathematical and implementation consistency through corrected summation bounds and OPQ specifications. These provide a modest gain in support and clarity. The additions remain limited: new tests lack sample-size and uncertainty details, and MFU reporting remains inconsistent—Figure 7 labels the 24.06-percentage-point difference as a percentage while Section 4.3 retains the 700.38% relative-improvement claim.
